item.title: Açúcar sobe e café cai na bolsa ICE, à medida que fundamentos prevalecem após eleições no Brasil
item.description: Os preços do açúcar subiram nesta terça-feira, enquanto o café arábica registrava queda, à medida que fatores fundamentais voltaram a influenciar os dois mercados, que haviam sofrido forte queda na sessão anterior, após a vitória eleitoral surpreendente do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva no Brasil.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Os preços do açúcar subiram nesta terça-feira, enquanto o café arábica registrava queda, à medida que fatores fundamentais voltaram a influenciar os dois mercados, que haviam sofrido forte queda na sessão anterior, após a vitória eleitoral surpreendente do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva no Brasil. A vitória de Lula provocou uma queda acentuada do real brasileiro , um cenário que incentiva as usinas, os produtores e os exportadores brasileiros a venderem contratos futuros de açúcar e café cotados em dólares, pois isso aumenta os retornos em moeda local. A moeda do maior produtor mundial de açúcar e café se estabilizou desde então, à medida que a poeira baixava após a eleição. O real era negociado a cerca de 5,35 por dólar na terça-feira, cerca de 7% abaixo do nível anterior à eleição, mas em melhor situação do que na segunda-feira, quando chegou a cair 12%. Os futuros de açúcar bruto na ICE , considerados uma referência global de preços, fecharam com alta de 0,5% nesta terça-feira, a 19,20 centavos por libra-peso, após terem fechado com queda de 5,6% na segunda-feira. Os futuros de café arábica da ICE , por outro lado, fecharam em queda de 7,2 centavos, ou 2,4%, a US$ 2,9375 por libra-peso, ampliando a queda de 2,1% registrada na segunda-feira. "Analisando os fundamentos do açúcar, as chuvas continuam custando dias de moagem (ao Brasil), e a Índia entra em seu pico de demanda festiva com estoques reduzidos, com os preços domésticos subindo em direção à paridade de importação. Portanto, esperamos que o mercado se recupere", afirmou a corretora de açúcar físico Deepcore. As perspectivas de oferta do café arábica, por outro lado, continuam a melhorar. "O clima para o café no Brasil continua chuvoso, mas favorável, apoiando a floração e o desenvolvimento inicial da safra, ao mesmo tempo em que acelera as expectativas de uma safra potencialmente recorde", disse o corretor independente Michael J Nugent. Ele acrescentou que os temores do mercado sobre o que a vitória de Lula poderia significar para a economia e a moeda brasileiras provavelmente foram exagerados logo após a vitória de Lula. "A expectativa convencional de uma deterioração acentuada nas relações entre os EUA e o Brasil pode se revelar simplista demais. Trump e Lula são, ambos, políticos altamente transacionais e práticos, que sabem como negociar", disse ele. O preço do açúcar branco subiu 0,7%, para US$519,20 por tonelada, após fechar com queda de 3,6% na segunda-feira, enquanto o preço do café robusta subiu 0,6%, para US$3.220 por tonelada, após registrar queda de 1,3% na segunda-feira. O robusta está sob pressão geral, à medida que a colheita começa no Vietnã, principal produtor, e os estoques nas bolsas continuam a aumentar. O cacau de Londres fechou com alta de £81, ou 1,9%, a £4.344 por tonelada, enquanto o cacau de Nova York subiu 1,6%, para US$ 5.577 por tonelada. (Reportagem de May Angel e Marcelo Teixeira)

item.title: Coca-Cola raises profit forecast as premium drinks, sodas hold strong
item.description: Coca-Cola has lifted its annual profit forecast, driven by robust demand for a range of beverages, particularly zero-sugar options. The company now anticipates earnings per share growth of at least 9% by 2026. Their third-quarter revenue soared to $13.38 billion, exceeding analysts' expectations, while Coca-Cola's strong showing stands in sharp contrast to PepsiCo's recent downgrades and cost-cutting plans. Following these promising results, Coca-Cola shares rose nearly 1% in premarket trading.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Coca-Cola on Tuesday raised its annual profit forecast, betting on resilient demand for its zero-sugar sodas and pricier beverages such as fairlife milk and sparkling soft drinks.The company now expects comparable currency-neutral earnings per share to grow at least 9% in 2026, up from its previous forecast of 7% to 8%.Coca-Cola's third-quarter revenue rose 7.4% to $13.38 billion, beating analysts' estimate of $12.92 billion, according to data compiled by LSEG.As high food and fuel prices make consumers more selective, Coca-Cola has sought to sustain demand by offering smaller, cheaper packs while rolling out pricier new flavours such as Coca-Cola Cherry Float.The company also benefited from demand during the soccer World Cup in July, including a brief sales boost for its energy drink brands.Its performance contrasts with rival PepsiCo, which lowered its annual targets earlier this month and stepped up cost cuts as it grapples with weak demand for snacks in North America.Coca-Cola shares rose nearly 1% in premarket trading. The stock has jumped about 33% in 2026 and is on track for a third straight year of gains, despite broader weakness in consumer spending and market volatility stemming from the war in Iran.

item.title: オレシュキで局地停戦開始、ロ・ウ双方が発表 キーウなどでは攻撃継続
item.description:
Dan Peleschuk Anna Voitenko
[キーウ ２７日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Dan Peleschuk　Anna Voitenko

[キーウ ２７日 ロイター] - ロシアとウクライナは２７日、ロシアが占領するウクライナ南部ヘルソン州オレシュキでの人道支援活動を可能にするため局地的な停戦を開始した。停戦により食料・医薬品不足が深刻なオレシュキへの支援物資搬入や住民の避難が可能になる。ただ、首都キーウなど他の地域では攻撃が続いている。

ロシアとウクライナはともに、前線に位置するオレシュ周辺での停戦を順守していると表明した。停戦はウクライナ時間午前３時（０１００ＧＭＴ、日本時間午前１０時）に発効し、１１月１日まで続く予定。

オレシュキは２０２２年２月からロシア占領下にあり、食料支援が滞るなどして住民の人道危機が深刻化。ホワイトハウスは先週、トランプ米大統領のメラニア夫人がオレシュキでの停戦実現に貢献したと発表した。

一方、キーウ市当局によると、２７日の新たな攻撃で市内の南橋と地下鉄インフラが被害を受けて通行や運行が停止、少なくとも１人が死亡した。

＜ロシアによる占領＞

オレシュキはウクライナ南部ヘルソン州のドニプロ川東岸に位置し、対岸にはウクライナ軍が支配するヘルソン市がある。ロシア軍は２２年２月の全面侵攻開始直後に制圧、支配を続けている。オレシュキは戦争での広範な被害のほか、２３年に付近のカホフカダムが破壊された際には、洪水でも甚大な被害を受けた。

米国によると、戦前２万４０００人だった人口は、現在わずか数千人に減っている。住民や当局者は、食料や医薬品、その他の生活必需品が深刻に不足していると報告。水道や電気、ガス、地域暖房の供給もほぼ途絶えている。食料や水を手に入れるだけのために住民は地雷が散在する道路を移動している状況だ。

ウクライナとロシアの当局者は、支援物資の搬入と住民の移動を可能にする人道回廊を設置すると表明。道路の地雷除去が必要になるとみられ、数日かかる可能性がある。

ウクライナとロシアは、オレシュキの人道危機の責任を互いに非難している。民間人にとって最大の脅威はドローンで、同市は両軍の無人機が容易に到達できる範囲にある。

＜キーウに新たな攻撃＞

ロシアによる夜間の攻撃ではキーウの重要な橋である南橋が被害を受けた。ゼレンスキー氏は、ウクライナの物流網に対する「攻撃の深刻な激化」だと述べた。ウクライナ軍関係者によると、南橋には弾道ミサイル「イスカンデル」４発が命中した。

ゼレンスキー氏によると、ほかの１０地域でも夜間にエネルギー施設や物流拠点、インフラが攻撃された。

ロシア国防省は、軍事目標を狙った攻撃で、キーウの交通インフラ、ハルキウ州の物流拠点のほか、産業施設や貨物船を攻撃したと発表した。

ロシアでは、ウクライナとの国境に近い西部ブリャンスク市でドローン攻撃により１人が死亡したと当局が発表した。ウクライナのザポリージャ州のロシア支配地域ではバスが攻撃され、当局者によると１人が死亡、３０人が負傷した。

item.title: India Deploys Extra Forces After Protests Over Dam on Chinese Border Escalate
item.description: By Tora Agarwala India has deployed hundreds of additional security personnel in its remote northeast, authorities said on Tuesday, after youth protesters clashed with police last week over a plan to build a mega-dam to counter a Chinese hydropower project upstream. Protests in Arunachal Pradesh’s …
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded:
By Tora Agarwala

India has deployed hundreds of additional security personnel in its remote northeast, authorities said on Tuesday, after youth protesters clashed with police last week over a plan to build a mega-dam to counter a Chinese hydropower project upstream.

Protests in Arunachal Pradesh’s Siang Valley, which borders Tibet, turned violent last week, triggering clashes with police, who made at least 21 arrests.

Police fired tear gas shells, while youth protesters pelted stones and set fire to a police station and an office of the state-owned National Hydroelectric Power Corporation, authorities said.

“Forces are being increased in the places where it is required. We do not want any law and order problem,” SD Singh Jamwal, police chief of Arunachal Pradesh, told Reuters.

Sporadic protests have taken place in the Siang Valley over the last two years, home to the proposed 11,200-megawatt Siang Upper Multipurpose Project, which will be developed by the state-run National Hydroelectric Power Corporation.

Villagers who oppose the project fear that the dam would submerge ancestral villages belonging to the Adi tribe.

“We will keep opposing this dam till they cancel it. If it is constructed, 27 of our ancestral villages will be completely submerged. At least 40 or 50 more will be affected,” Gegong Jijong of the Siang Indigenous Farmers’ Forum told Reuters.

The Siang River flows into Arunachal Pradesh from Tibet, where it is known as the Yarlung Zangbo. China announced plans in December 2024 to build the world’s largest hydropower dam upstream, triggering fears in New Delhi that its longtime strategic rival could weaponize its control of the river.

China claims Arunachal Pradesh, which it calls Zangnan, as part of southern Tibet. India says the state is an integral and inalienable part of its territory.

Arunachal Pradesh’s chief minister, a member of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Bharatiya Janata Party, has called the Chinese project an existential threat and said the government would protect national interests while respecting the rights and aspirations of the people of Siang Valley.

item.title: Boeing shares sell off on slower-than-expected 737 production, weaker free cash flow outlook
item.description: Boeing CEO Kelly Ortberg said on Tuesday that the company will miss its 737 production and jet delivery targets this year, dealing a setback to its recovery and sending shares tumbling nearly 10%, their worst day in more than 18 months.
item.dc:creator: Dan Catchpole, Shivansh Tiwary
item.content:encoded: Boeing (BA.N) CEO Kelly Ortberg said on Tuesday that the company will miss its 737 production and jet delivery targets this year, dealing a setback to its recovery and sending shares tumbling nearly 10%, their worst day in more than 18 months. The company also said it expects free cash flow to grow slower than analysts expected, reaching its $10 billion target in 2029, a year later than investors' consensus, according to LSEG data. While many aerospace companies are struggling to increase output, Boeing is recovering from [USN:L2N3OO01G TEXT:"years of crises and controversies"] that dented its reputation, drained cash and saddled it with a heavy debt load. That may make investors more inclined to sell shares, even though Boeing's long-term outlook remains good due to high demand for jetliners and only one major competitor, Europe's Airbus (AIR.PA) , said Tony Bancroft, an investment analyst with Gabelli Funds investment group. The market is going to punish any delay in increasing cash flow, he said. Boeing expects to generate $3 billion next year, lower than Wall Street's consensus projection of $5.5 billion due to lower deliveries and higher capital investment, Jefferies analyst Sheila Kahyaoglu said in a research note on Tuesday. The company posted free cash flow of $464 million in the most recent quarter; for the year so far it has burned through $359 million in cash, but it still expects to generate $2 billion by the end of the year. Boeing reported an adjusted loss of 34 cents per share for the quarter through September, compared with an expected loss of 21 cents, according to data compiled by LSEG. Shares were down 9.6% to $170.23 in afternoon trading, which would be the stock's worst day since April 3, 2025. PRODUCTION STRUGGLES Boeing now expects to reach its 737 production rate target of 47 jets a month in early 2027. As recently as May, Boeing executives said they would hit that pace [USN:FWN4240QK TEXT:"this summer"]. As a result, Boeing will not reach its 500-jet delivery target this year, the company's financial chief Jay Malave said during a conference call with analysts on Tuesday. Wing production continues to be a major constraint, but Boeing still plans to increase to 52 jets a month in the second half of 2027, Ortberg said on the call. To reach that rate, Boeing needs to be producing five jets a month at its new 737 production line in Everett, Washington, which [USN:L6N437087 TEXT:"opened in July"], and increase fuselage production at the former Spirit AeroSystems plant in Wichita, Kansas. Boeing bought Spirit last year in part due to significant ongoing manufacturing defects. Currently, Boeing is making fuselages at a lower rate while it uses up its existing inventory. Starting now, it has to increase output at Wichita to be in line with 737 output, Ortberg said. Deliveries of the popular single-aisle jetliner are a major driver of Boeing's cash flow, and before Ortberg joined Boeing in 2024, the company had struggled for years with production problems due to rushing rate increases at the expense of quality. Despite pressure to increase 737 output faster, "we're going to be smart about this, stay disciplined, and the outlook is there," Ortberg said. The company continues to struggle with production challenges in its 787 program and a supplier dispute has stalled wing production for 777 freighters and 767s, which includes the KC-46 aerial refueling tanker, as [USN:L6N46911Z TEXT:"first reported by Reuters"] on Friday. Shipments for wing production have resumed, but the disruption will show up "over the next few quarters," Malave said. Boeing expects the 777-9 jetliner will be on track for regulator certification by mid-2027, with 10 to 15 deliveries next year. LARGER-THAN-EXPECTED QUARTERLY LOSS The dimmer outlook and a larger-than-expected quarterly loss overshadowed major wins by Boeing in recent months: certification by US regulators of the [USN:S0N42W0AH TEXT:"737 MAX 7"] and [USN:L1N4660WQ TEXT:"MAX 10"] and winning the US Navy's sixth-generation F/A-XX [USN:L6N45R0R4 TEXT:"fighter contract"]. "Expectations are rising, and they should. We have a stronger foundation than a year ago, but we also have more work to do to deliver on our backlog, strengthen our culture, and improve how we work every day," Ortberg said in a memo to employees after the results. Revenue at Boeing's commercial airplanes division dipped slightly to $10.7 billion, while the operating loss stood at $697 million for an operating margin of negative 6.5%, compared with negative 48.3% a year ago. The company attributed the performance to less profitable jetliner deliveries and higher production costs, including from its supply chain. At Boeing's defense division, higher deliveries, improved operational performance and a $252-million sale of subsidiary HRL Laboratories contributed to nearly $500 million in quarterly earnings with an operating margin of 6.2%, up from 1.7% a year ago. Boeing Global Services earned $1 billion and posted an operating margin of 18.3%. The US planemaker ended the quarter with $25.2 billion in net debt, down slightly from $25.9 billion at the close of the previous quarter and $30.4 billion a year ago. (This story has been corrected to change the analyst's name to Tony Bancroft, not Tony Gabelli, in paragraph 4.)

item.title: ＧＭ、ＮＹＳＥからナスダックに上場先移管 11月17日から
item.description: [２７日 ロイター] - 米自動車大手のゼネラル・モーターズは２７日、普通株式の上場先をニューヨーク証券取引所（ＮＹ...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ＧＭ、ＮＹＳＥからナスダックに上場先移管　11月17日から 10/27 20:32 配信

ゼネラル・モーターズのロゴ、デトロイトの新本社ビルで1月12日撮影 REUTERS/Rebecca Cook/File Photo（ロイター） [２７日 ロイター] - 米自動車大手のゼネラル・モーターズは２７日、普通株式の上場先をニューヨーク証券取引所（ＮＹＳＥ）からナスダックに移管すると発表した。

１１月１７日からナスダック市場で取引を開始する見込み。現在のティッカーシンボルは維持する。ＬＳＥＧデータによると、ＧＭの時価総額は約６４４億ドル。

ハイテク株の多いナスダックとの結び付きを求めて上場先を移す企業が増えておりＧＭも仲間入りをする。

ウォルマート、ヒルトン、パランティアなども最近ナスダックに上場先を移管、移管方針を公表している。

ポール・ジェイコブソン最高財務責任者（ＣＦＯ）は「顧客を中心に据え、技術を原動力とするＧＭの戦略は株主に価値を生み出している。成長を続ける上でナスダックは自然な上場先だ」と述べた。

ＧＭの株価は寄り前の取引で約２％上昇した。

item.description: [フランクフルト ２７日 ロイター] - 欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）が２７日公表したデータによると、ユーロ圏の銀行融資は９...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ユーロ圏9月銀行融資、堅調維持　銀行の融資姿勢厳格化でも 10/27 20:24 配信

フランクフルトの金融街、2019年撮影 REUTERS/Kai Pfaffenbach（ロイター） [フランクフルト ２７日 ロイター] - 欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）が２７日公表したデータによると、ユーロ圏の銀行融資は９月も堅調な伸びを維持した。金利上昇や地政学的な混乱を背景に、銀行が融資姿勢を厳しくする中でも伸びが続いた。

融資の伸びは企業向けが４．２％、家計向けが３．１％と、いずれも８月と同水準だった。

一方、ＥＣＢの四半期銀行融資調査では、住宅ローン需要が減少し、融資も受けにくくなるなど、利上げの影響が表れ始めていることが分かった。

第３・四半期に住宅ローンの需要が減少したと報告した銀行は、差し引き２７％だった。銀行の予想（マイナス１２％）や４─６月期の実績（マイナス１５％）を上回る落ち込みだった。

ＥＣＢは「金利上昇が需要減少の主因で、次いで消費者信頼感の低下と住宅市場の見通し悪化が要因だった」と分析した。

銀行は第３・四半期に住宅ローンの融資基準を厳格化しなかったが、企業向け融資と消費者信用では厳しくした。第４・四半期には全ての融資で基準を厳格化する見通しだ。

欧州主要国の中で融資基準の厳格化が最も顕著だったのはフランスだった。

ＥＣＢは「リスクへの警戒感の高まりと銀行のリスク許容度の低下が、引き続き融資基準厳格化の主因だった。一部の銀行は、地政学的な不確実性やエネルギーを巡る動向による圧力が強まっていると報告した」と説明した。

ロイター 関連リンク アングル：ＴＯＰＩＸ銘柄入れ替え・比率変更、期日接近でリバランス活発化 アングル：債券市場の混乱やインフレ、為替変動がアジア系銀行を圧迫　収益と資本にリスク 焦点：主要生保の26年度下期、円債は入れ替え中心　金利上昇には最終局面の見方 焦点：米経済へのＡＩ効果、潜在成長率への波及は不透明 コラム：ＩＭＦが指摘する「薄氷のＡＩ相場」、日本も逆資産効果に備える時か＝唐鎌大輔氏 10/27(火) 20:24 最終更新 ロイター

item.title: 中国習主席、福田元首相の遺族に弔電 日中友好への貢献評価
item.description: [北京 ２７日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[北京 ２７日 ロイター] - 中国の習近平国家主席は２７日、２２日に９０歳で死去した福田康夫元首相の遺族に弔電を送った。

国営新華社通信によると、習氏は福田氏について、誠実さと責任感を備えた日本の政治家であり、中国人民の古くからの友人でもあったと述べた。

「（福田氏は）長年にわたり中日友好に深い関心を寄せ、正しい歴史認識を堅持した」と評価した。福田氏が日中関係とアジアの発展に果たした貢献を中国は忘れないと述べた。

「日本の現在の指導者が前の世代の政治家の努力を大切にし、中日間の４つの政治文書を順守して、両国関係の政治的基盤をしっかりと守ることを望む」と表明した。

item.title: Ares Capital seals $2.6 billion deal for Apollo's MFIC as consolidation continues
item.description: Ares Capital said on Tuesday it will buy Apollo's MidCap Financial Investment Corp in a $2.6 billion cash-and-stock deal, adding to growing consolidation among publicly traded private credit funds.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ares Capital (ARCC.O) said on Tuesday it will buy Apollo's MidCap Financial Investment Corp (MFIC.O) in a $2.6 billion cash-and-stock deal, adding to growing consolidation among publicly traded private credit funds. The acquisition strengthens Ares Capital's presence in direct lending to mid-sized businesses and expands its portfolio to more than 800 companies across a broader range of industries and financial sponsors. MidCap shareholders will receive $10.88 per fully diluted share, comprising about $1.21 in cash and $9.67 in Ares Capital stock. The offer represents a premium of more than 30% to MidCap stock's Monday close. MidCap shares jumped more than 24%. BlackRock TCP Capital (TCPC.O) , Investcorp Credit Management BDC (ICMB.O) , and WhiteHorse Finance (WHF.O) have all said this year they are weighing strategic options, suggesting consolidation among publicly traded private credit funds could pick up. The vehicles are [USN:L6N3ZZ0TU TEXT:"trading"] at steep discounts to net asset value as investors question the quality of the loans the funds have made. With the acquisition, Ares Capital will have bought all three of the largest business development companies (BDCs) that were operating at the time of its 2004 IPO, Ares Capital CEO Kort Schnabel said, adding that the firm is well positioned to pursue further opportunities as they emerge. "We have consistently used periods of market volatility and dislocation to create differentiated opportunities for our shareholders while building greater scale," Schnabel added. Ares Capital is the largest publicly traded BDC — vehicles that give investors access to a diversified pool of private credit assets — by market capitalization. "ARCC has had a successful track record of acquiring challenged BDC portfolios at a discount to NAV (Allied Capital, American Capital) and the MFIC transaction would seem similar to us," RBC analyst Kenneth Lee said. For Apollo, the deal marks another step in streamlining its portfolio of publicly traded investment vehicles. The deal is expected to close in the first half of 2027 and boost Ares Capital's core earnings per share. Wells Fargo advised Ares Capital and is providing $750 million in financing for the deal. Moelis advised MidCap's special committee.

item.title: Auditor of GFG Alliance's Liberty Commodities fined in UK
item.description: Britain's auditing watchdog has fined an accounting firm and an accountant for failing to show enough professional scepticism when auditing Liberty Commodities Ltd (LCL), in its latest penalty related to metals magnate Sanjeev Gupta's GFG Alliance.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Britain's auditing watchdog has fined an accounting firm and an accountant for failing to show enough professional scepticism when auditing Liberty Commodities Ltd (LCL), in its latest penalty related to metals magnate Sanjeev Gupta's GFG Alliance. Auditor HW Fisher has been fined £140,000 ($186,500) and handed a "severe reprimand" for the LCL audit to March 31, 2020, the Financial Reporting Council (FRC) said on Tuesday Simon Mott-Cowan, who voluntarily ceased his audit practice at the end of 2025, has been fined £17,500 and issued with a "severe reprimand" over the same audit HW Fisher and Mott-Cowan did not immediately respond to requests for comment Fines were reduced by 30% after cooperation LCL dealt with physical trading, supply chain and logistics management of non-ferrous metals, semi-finished steel and raw materials required for steelmaking Audit breaches were numerous and serious but not intentional, dishonest, deliberate or reckless, the FRC said. It did not say financial statements were misstated The FRC has [USN:L1N42V0DL TEXT:"sanctioned a number of accountants"] in Britain over audits of companies in the GFG Alliance Gupta was once dubbed the "saviour of steel." But the failure in March 2021 of GFG's main lender, Greensill Capital, prompted a scramble to refinance. The UK Serious Fraud Office opened a fraud, fraudulent trading and [USN:L8N2N122U TEXT:"money laundering investigation"] into GFG two months later GFG has denied wrongdoing and said last year that it had struck a deal with Greensill creditors on global debt settlement terms ($1 = 0.7505 pounds)

item.title: Yemen's Houthis say they hit Saudi Ras Tanura oil refinery with missile
item.description: Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis said on Tuesday they had hit Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura oil refinery, the biggest in the kingdom, with a ballistic missile.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis said on Tuesday they had hit Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura oil refinery, the biggest in the kingdom, with a ballistic missile. Intensifying hostilities between Yemen and Saudi Arabia have further disrupted oil supplies and heightened the risk of a wider regional conflict, eight months since the Iran war began. The Houthis also said they had attacked Saudi military aircraft and repelled an advance by Saudi-backed forces near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, an important Red Sea shipping route. The Houthis' military spokesperson, Yahya Saree, said the strike on the Ras Tanura refinery had caused a fire at the complex, which also includes a shipping terminal and is located on the Gulf, west of the Strait of Hormuz. Saudi authorities did not immediately confirm the strike. Ras Tanura, which has a capacity of 550,000 barrels per day, was shut for a period in the early months of the Iran war as a precautionary measure. Nearly all Saudi Arabia's oil exports flow through two main ports: Ras Tanura in the Gulf and Yanbu on the Red Sea, both of which the Houthis have attacked in the past. Bloomberg News cited a person familiar with the matter as saying Saudi Arabia had contained a fire near Ras Tanura's terminal. AIRSTRIKES The Houthis said they had attacked two military transport jets at Najran Airport and an airbase in Khamis Mushait. They also said they attacked the Saudi defence ministry building in Riyadh, and Abha airport. There was no immediate Saudi confirmation of the attacks. On Tuesday afternoon, civil defence authorities briefly issued an air raid alert in the Saudi capital Riyadh. Falling debris from the interception of two ballistic missiles over Riyadh caused material damage to a building, a construction site and a vehicle, the Saudi Civil Defence said later on Tuesday. The Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis in support of Yemen's internationally recognised government said it had intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles launched by the Houthis towards Riyadh. The Houthis said they had repelled an advance by forces they described as Saudi-backed from the southern approaches to the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces earlier this month [USN:L1N45R06H TEXT:"pushed the Houthis out"] of coastal areas they had seized in September, loosening the group's grip on a vital Red Sea oil route. Houthi-affiliated Al Masirah TV reported Saudi strikes on the Yemeni city of Mocha. There was no immediate Saudi confirmation. The fighting has shattered a 2022 UN-brokered truce between the coalition and the Houthis, who control the Yemeni capital Sanaa. On Monday, Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan [USN:S8N4320AV TEXT:"met Iranian officials"] in Tehran to try to reduce regional tensions. Parliament in Egypt, which has said it is considering joining the three countries in a mutual defence pact, authorised Egypt's military on Monday to help defend Saudi Arabia if asked.

item.description:
Olesya Astakhova Ahmad Ghaddar
[モスクワ／ロンドン ２７日] - 石油輸出国機構（ＯＰ...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ＯＰＥＣプラス、12月の生産目標据え置きへ＝関係筋 10/27 20:03 配信

ウィーンの石油輸出国機構（ＯＰＥＣ）本部、2024年撮影 REUTERS/Leonhard Foeger/File Photo（ロイター） Olesya Astakhova　Ahmad Ghaddar

[モスクワ／ロンドン ２７日] - 石油輸出国機構（ＯＰＥＣ）と非加盟の主要な産油国で構成する「ＯＰＥＣプラス」は、１１月１日の会合で１２月の原油生産目標を据え置く公算が大きい。関係者３人がロイターに明らかにした。最終決定には至っていないという。

オンライン会合にはサウジアラビア、ロシア、イラク、クウェート、アルジェリア、カザフスタン、オマーンの主要７カ国が参加する。

ＯＰＥＣプラスは２０２３年に当初合意した日量１６５万バレルの減産の段階的な解除を９月に完了した。ただ大半の加盟国を対象とする日量約２００万バレルの減産が２６年末まで残っている。

関係者によると、ＯＰＥＣプラスは２７年の基準生産量を設定する前に、加盟国の生産能力の検証を終える必要がある。基準生産量は今後の生産割当量を決める基準となり、残る減産の解除計画にも影響する。

イラン戦争による混乱で湾岸産油国の生産量は割当量を下回っている。

item.title: Coca-Cola lifts profit forecast on international soda demand, flags higher costs
item.description: Coca-Cola on Tuesday raised its annual profit forecast as soft drink demand held up in markets including India and Brazil, even as it warned of accelerating cost pressures and persistent consumer weakness into 2027.
item.dc:creator: Juveria Tabassum, Alexander Marrow
item.content:encoded: Coca-Cola on Tuesday raised its annual profit forecast as soft drink demand held up in markets including India and Brazil, even as it warned of accelerating cost pressures and persistent consumer weakness into 2027. The company has sought to win over increasingly selective consumers with smaller, cheaper packs in the United States, while also rolling out pricier offerings such as Coca-Cola Cherry Float. But like other consumer goods companies, Coca-Cola faces higher packaging and freight costs as the US war in Iran drives up commodity prices. The company said in July that aluminum and PET costs had risen more than expected this year. [USN:L6N45Z19G TEXT:"Diesel prices"] have jumped to record highs because of the war, pushing up freight and transport costs across industries. Consumer goods bellwether [USN:L4N46811U TEXT:"P&G"] last week raised its estimate of the hit from higher costs to its annual profit. Coca-Cola executives also warned that pressure on consumers could extend into 2027. CFO John Murphy pointed to weakness in the restaurant industry, which was a slight drag on North American volumes. "While our own business continues to have a lot of momentum ... I think the underlying pressure across the consumer landscape is there, and I think it will be there for the rest of the year as we go into 2027," Murphy said. Overall volumes rose about 5%, while prices increased about 1%. Packaged goods companies have also become more cautious about raising prices as consumers focus more sharply on affordability amid higher food and fuel costs. COSTS RISE, BUT MARGINS HOLD STEADY A 7.4% increase in third-quarter revenue helped support Coca-Cola's operating margin, which rose to 33.4%. Growth in India, China, Mexico and Brazil helped lift global unit case volumes as the company focused on local flavors and affordable packs in some markets, Coca-Cola said. North American volumes were flat, with growth in trademark Coca-Cola sodas and pricier beverages such as fairlife milk helping offset higher input costs and a production disruption earlier this year at its Topo Chico brand. Coca-Cola's volume growth across sodas and other beverage brands [USN:L6N44A0IM TEXT:"contrasts"] with rival [USN:L4N45U0P6 TEXT:"PepsiCo's"] struggles with weak US demand for its snacks and sodas. Coca-Cola now expects comparable currency-neutral earnings per share to grow at least 9% in 2026, up from its previous forecast of 7% to 8%. "The gap between Coke and peers is widening. As the market debates price increases, those delivering volume growth should outperform," Jefferies analyst Kaumil Gajrawala said. Revenue for the quarter ended October 2 reached $13.38 billion, beating analysts' estimate of $12.92 billion, according to LSEG data. Adjusted earnings of 91 cents per share also topped estimates of 88 cents. Coca-Cola's shares were down marginally in early trading. They are up about 33% this year.

item.title: El crudo baja 2 dólares por negociación en Oriente Medio que modera preocupación por oferta
item.description: Los futuros del petróleo cayeron casi 2 dólares por barril el martes, porque los operadores centraban su atención en las conversaciones de paz en Oriente Medio.
item.dc:creator: Georgina Mccartney
item.content:encoded: Los futuros del petróleo cayeron casi 2 dólares por barril el martes, porque los operadores centraban su atención en las conversaciones de paz en Oriente Medio. Sin embargo, los precios se mantenían cerca de los máximos de los últimos seis meses, debido a que el conflicto entre los hutíes y Arabia Saudita persistía y a los inversores les preocupaba la posibilidad de que se recrudezca la guerra de Estados Unidos e Israel contra Irán. Los futuros del crudo Brent bajaron 1,93 dólares, o un 1,67%, a 113,88 dólares el barril, mientras que el West Texas Intermediate de Estados Unidos cerraron con una caída de 1,86 dólares, o un 1,83%, a 99,90 dólares. El jefe del Consejo de Seguridad iraní, Mohsen Rezaei, se reunió el martes con el líder supremo, el ayatolá Mojtaba Jameneí, un día después de haber mantenido conversaciones con representantes de Arabia Saudita, Turquía y Pakistán. Medios estatales informaron de que Jameneí había hecho hincapié en la importancia de velar por los intereses de Irán y de mantener sus condiciones para poner fin a la guerra. Los cuatro países acordaron continuar las conversaciones con el objetivo de reforzar la cooperación en materia de paz y seguridad, dijeron los medios estatales iraníes. Las perspectivas de paz se han visto mermadas por los nuevos ataques de los hutíes yemeníes, alineados con Irán, contra Arabia Saudita, uno de los principales productores de petróleo. Los hutíes dijeron el martes que habían atacado con un misil balístico la refinería de petróleo de Ras Tanura, en Arabia Saudita, la mayor del reino. "Los continuos ataques hutíes contra Arabia Saudita y la creciente presencia militar en el Golfo mantienen los riesgos de suministro, aunque las noticias diplomáticas animen a que se reduzca parte de la prima reciente", dijeron los analistas de Gelber & Associates en una nota. Octubre ha sido el peor mes en cuanto a ataques contra el transporte marítimo comercial en el estrecho de Ormuz y las vías navegables cercanas, según datos recopilados por un centro de estudios de Washington, que lleva desde 2017 realizando un seguimiento de los incidentes de seguridad marítima en todo el mundo.

item.title: 防衛費増強、増税排除すべきでないとの声も 安保3文書改定の有識者会議
item.description:
Yoshifumi Takemoto
［東京 ２７日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Yoshifumi Takemoto

［東京　２７日　ロイター］ - 政府は２７日、国家安全保障戦略など安保関連３文書の改定に向けた有識者会議を開いた。政府側の説明によると、安定財源確保のため増税も選択肢から排除すべきではないとの意見が出た。ただ、具体的な税目や防衛費増額の数値目標については議論されなかった。

有識者会議の開催は今回で５回目。政府側によると、防衛力の強化を産業力の向上につなげ、経済の好循環を生み出す構想については幅広い賛同が得られた。防衛省は、新たな戦い方の実現に不可欠な人工知能（ＡＩ）、無人機（ドローン）、宇宙、サイバー分野は、高市早苗政権が掲げる危機管理と成長投資の方針に合致すると説明し、防衛産業を強化するための法人を設立する方針を示した。

岸田文雄政権以降、日本は米国などの意向も踏まえ、防衛費の対国内総生産（ＧＤＰ）比を１％から２％へ引き上げた。米国は同盟国に３．５％の水準を求めているが、今回の会議では「防衛費は積み上げの結果だ」との意見が出た一方、明確な数値目標に関する発言はなかったという。

防衛費の拡充を巡っては、「防衛以外の安保経費がまぶされないように」との意見も出た。また、日本が新たな軍国主義に向かっているとの批判が生じた場合を想定し、対応策を検討しておくべきだとの指摘もあった。非核三原則の見直しや原子力潜水艦の保有については議論されなかったという。

政府は年内に３文書を改定する方針だが、次回の有識者会議の日程は未定としている。

item.title: Dólar sube a medida que mercados centran la atención en reuniones de bancos centrales
item.description: El dólar se fortaleció el martes frente a las principales divisas, entre ellas el euro, el yen y la libra esterlina, en un contexto de posicionamiento del mercado ante una serie de reuniones de los bancos centrales en las que se esperan nuevas pistas sobre las perspectivas económicas y la trayectoria de las tasas de interés.
item.dc:creator: Chibuike Oguh, Alun John
item.content:encoded: El dólar se fortaleció el martes frente a las principales divisas, entre ellas el euro, el yen y la libra esterlina, en un contexto de posicionamiento del mercado ante una serie de reuniones de los bancos centrales en las que se esperan nuevas pistas sobre las perspectivas económicas y la trayectoria de las tasas de interés. * El dólar también se ha estabilizado tras sufrir presiones a raíz de la ola de ventas que afectó la semana pasada a las acciones de empresas de inteligencia artificial, que venían registrando fuertes subidas. * El euro bajó un 0,33%, a 1,1136 dólares. * La Reserva Federal tiene previsto anunciar su última decisión de política monetaria el miércoles, el Banco Central Europeo lo hará el jueves y el Banco de Japón cerrará la semana el viernes. * Se espera que los tres mantengan las tasas sin cambios, por lo que la atención se centrará en cualquier indicio que den los responsables a cargo de la política monetaria sobre sus perspectivas. * El euro va camino de ser la divisa de los mercados desarrollados con peor comportamiento en octubre, con una caída del 1,70% frente al dólar, lastrado por los elevados costos energéticos, la volatilidad de los bonos del Estado francés y las preocupaciones sobre la situación fiscal de Francia. * La moneda única amplió ligeramente su caída tras la publicación de la Encuesta Trimestral sobre Préstamos Bancarios del BCE, que puso de manifiesto que el impacto de sus subidas de tasas está empezando a hacerse notar. Si esa tendencia continúa, podría, en cierta medida, reducir la presión sobre el BCE para que continúe con las subidas de tasas hasta bien entrado el próximo año. * Por su parte, la ministra de Finanzas de Japón, Satsuki Katayama, afirmó que el gobierno está preparado para tomar medidas decisivas en el mercado de divisas, recordando a los mercados su disposición a intervenir para respaldar su moneda. * El yen fue una de las divisas principales con mejor comportamiento la semana pasada, apreciándose alrededor de un 0,75% frente al dólar, su mayor subida semanal desde principios de septiembre, ya que el nerviosismo en torno a la IA en el mercado de valores provocó una fuga hacia la divisa. * El dólar subió un 0,24%, a 157,90 yenes japoneses . La libra esterlina cedió un 0,19%, a 1,3317 dólares. * El índice dólar , que mide la evolución de la moneda estadounidense frente a una cesta de seis divisas que incluye el yen y el euro, ganó un 0,27%, a 102,29.

item.title: イスラエルの「スパイ企業」、スターリンクユーザー標的＝関係筋
item.description:
Raphael Satter
[ワシントン ２７日 ロイター] - サイバーセキュリティー企業トレンドマイクロの子会社...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
イスラエルの「スパイ企業」、スターリンクユーザー標的＝関係筋 10/27 19:34 配信

イーロン・マスク氏のシルエットとスターリンクのロゴ REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration/File Photo（ロイター） Raphael Satter

[ワシントン ２７日 ロイター] - サイバーセキュリティー企業トレンドマイクロの子会社「TrendAI」の専門家は最近、イスラエルの広告技術企業Discover-Techが米スペースＸの衛星通信網「スターリンク」 利用者を標的に「スパイ行為」を行っていた可能性があることを確認した。事情に詳しい関係筋６人が明らかにした。

Discover-Techはスターリンクサービスユーザーに表示されるデジタル広告の大手の１つで、これらの広告がユーザーの位置情報を特定するために使用されている可能性が高いという。

研究者らは、Discover-Techがスターリンクユーザーをターゲットとした広告の世界有数の入札者となり、スターリンク自体が禁止または制限されている国を含む１００カ国以上でスターリンクトラフィックの首位入札者になっていることを発見した。

スペースＸはコメント要請に応じなかった。Discover-Techもコメント要請に応じていない。

TrendAIは今月１５日にスターリンクユーザーが標的となっていることに関するリポートを公表したが、Discover-Techの名前は挙げず、代わりに「Shadow-Earth-７９」と呼ばれる「広告技術企業」が責任者だと指摘。関係筋６人によると、Shadow-Earth-７９はTrendAIがDiscover-Techに対して用いたコードネーム。

TrendAIは、なぜリポートでShadow-Earth-７９を社名で特定しなかったのかという質問には直接答えず、属性に関する自社のアプローチは誤りのリスクを減らすことなどを目的としていると声明で述べた。

TrendAIがShadow-Earth-７９に関するリポートを発表したのと同じ日に、カナダのサイバー監視団体シチズン・ラボとニューヨークの広告テクノロジー企業コンフィアントはDiscover-Techを名指し。両グループは同社が広告入札プロセスを悪用し、インターネットユーザーに関するデータを漏えいさせたと主張。漏えいしたデータを収集・照合して他の情報と統合することで、ユーザーの匿名性を解除し、ウェブ上での行動を追跡し、場合によっては監視ソフトウエアによる標的設定を行うことができるようになる。

シチズン・ラボとコンフィアントは、これらの広告がメディア組織、政府機関、テクノロジー企業が所有する数十の機密ネットワーク内で表示されていたと述べた。

調査を受けて、グーグル、コムキャストなどの企業は、Discover-Techを自社の広告プラットフォームから排除したと発表した。

関係筋の１人と、この件に詳しい７人目の関係筋によると、少なくとも米国の大手テクノロジー企業１社と１つの国際機関が最近、Discover-Techの広告が自社の従業員をターゲットにしていたかどうかについて、内部調査を開始した。

ロイター 関連リンク アングル：ネタニヤフ氏、旧来の選挙戦術で「守護者」演出　ハマス攻撃で信頼回復に苦戦も コラム：中東紛争、サウジ皇太子が「ワイルドカード」　対応読みづらく コラム：石油価格、イラン攻撃による急騰から持久戦へ 焦点：経済的圧力強化で苦境のイラン、米国期待の譲歩はなお不透明 アングル：欧州天然ガス在庫が過去最低水準、冬場の調達コスト高騰リスクも 10/27(火) 19:34 最終更新 ロイター

item.title: China hands former security regulator anti-graft official suspended death sentence
item.description: A Chinese court on Tuesday handed Wang Huimin, a former anti-graft official at the China Securities Regulatory Commission, a death sentence with a two-year reprieve over corruption and said Wang illegally accepted more than 436 million yuan ($65 million).
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A Chinese court on Tuesday handed Wang Huimin, a former anti-graft official at the China Securities Regulatory Commission, a death sentence with a two-year reprieve over corruption and said Wang illegally accepted more than 436 million yuan ($65 million). Wang accepted bribes in exchange for favours to companies and individuals, including help with business operations and fundraising, while holding a number of official posts in the northwestern region of Xinjiang and at the national securities regulator from 1998 to 2025, state-run Xinhua news agency said, citing a first-instance judgement The court said Wang's "exceptionally large" bribes and the severe harm caused warranted the death penalty, but gave him a two-year reprieve because, among other considerations, some offences were only attempted, he voluntarily disclosed some facts not previously known to investigators and some illicit gains were recovered He admitted guilt and expressed remorse in court, Xinhua said The court also deprived him of political rights for life and ordered the confiscation of all his personal property The suspended death sentence in Chinese law gives a convict a two-year reprieve from execution, after which the sentence is typically commuted to life imprisonment The court said Wang would spend the rest of his life in prison, with no possibility of sentence reduction or parole ($1 = 6.6680 Chinese yuan renminbi)

item.title: Fashion's AI era: face swaps and digital clones
item.description: LONDON, Oct 27 : AI-generated fashion models present a tantalizing opportunity for brands: the ability to create lifelike images for their retail websites while cutting costs by 90 per cent or more compared to photo shoots with human models.For the modeling industry, the technology poses an existential threat
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:
Advertisement

Business

Fashion's AI era: face swaps and digital clones

FILE PHOTO: People walk past the L’Oreal booth during the World Artificial Intelligence Conference (WAIC) in Shanghai, China, July 17, 2026. REUTERS/Go Nakamura

Head of the British Fashion Model Agents Association (BFMA) John Horner poses for a photograph during an interview with Reuters, in London, Britain, July 2, 2026. REUTERS/Isabel Infantes

Head of the British Fashion Model Agents Association (BFMA) John Horner poses for a photograph during an interview with Reuters, in London, Britain, July 2, 2026. REUTERS/Isabel Infantes

FILE PHOTO: Clothing by Calvin Klein, a brand owned by PVH Corp., is pictured for sale in a store in Manhattan, New York City, U.S., November 30, 2021. REUTERS/Andrew Kelly/File Photo

FAST

LONDON, Oct 27 : AI-generated fashion models present a tantalizing opportunity for brands: the ability to create lifelike images for their retail websites while cutting costs by 90 per cent or more compared to photo shoots with human models. For the modeling industry, the technology poses an existential threat because of scant regulation governing the ownership or use of digital twins. Fashion models face the risk of unpaid replication of their image – or replacement by entirely synthetic models. To understand how AI is upending the economics of fashion modeling, Reuters interviewed 15 model-agency directors and reviewed more than a dozen confidential photo-shoot contracts in which brands including Diesel, Calvin Klein and L'Oreal detailed proposed terms for AI-created alterations and future use of the images. The companies’ contract requests included the right to swap a model's face with another using AI; the creation of a digital clone with no additional compensation to the model; and the right to use images of a model's body to train AI. The terms in the unsigned contracts also included broad legal language that could effectively give a brand leeway to use AI however it wanted.

While some companies are looking to repurpose or modify images of existing models, others are using fully AI-generated models, not based on existing humans. As AI use expands, modeling agencies are seeing bookings decline, photo studios are closing and models are facing the loss of a chunk of their livelihoods: photo shoots by fast-fashion retailers constantly adding new collections to their websites. "Within a year, even the next six months, there's going to be less jobs for models, especially our bread and butter, which is ecommerce," said Adot Gak, a model based in London who has been on the cover of Harper's Bazaar and appeared in campaigns by brands including Balmain and H&M. "If we don't speak up about this, in the next two years the whole industry will just be bots." While some fast-fashion players like Spain’s Mango have already rolled out AI-generated models at scale, high-end brands are moving more cautiously. Moncler experimented early with an AI-generated campaign in 2023, and Gucci caused controversy in fashion circles when it posted images generated by AI on Instagram this year.  Moncler said it does not currently use AI-generated models, either on its website or in its campaigns. Gucci did not respond to requests for comment.  "The scariest part is that now people cannot differentiate between a real model and an AI model," said Gak. FACE SWAPS AND 'DIGITAL TWINS' AI allows retailers to endlessly rework and redeploy a model’s image wearing different outfits at a fraction of the cost of new shoots.  "Some brands ask to modify faces, bodies, skin, age or expressions after shoots using AI. Others are asking about creating 'digital twins' of models that they can reuse later without needing another production," said Patrick Staal, owner of modeling agency Uniko Models in Barcelona. In a photo-shoot casting sheet, Italian brand Diesel asked models to agree to "alteration or reconstruction of facial features and body proportions,” along with “swapping of faces among the participating models,” and “superimposition of the Participant’s face onto another person’s body.” Diesel's parent company OTB told Reuters the model release was drafted for a specific campaign and isn’t representative of its typical agreements. It said it doesn’t systematically modify models with AI. Reale Actives – the skincare brand launched this year by social-media personality Alix Earle – uses the tagline, "Reale you is perfect you." But in a contract seen by Reuters, the brand asked for rights to create AI-generated replicas of models and to "own" and use these fakes for a year without further compensation. Reale Actives said in a statement that it uses real models and hasn’t replicated any model using AI. It said the contract language came from a partner production company, which it declined to name. MODELS TRAINING THEIR MACHINE REPLACEMENTS?  In some cases, models are helping to train their replacements: some contracts’ fine print includes language allowing the use of their images to train AI tools.  A Calvin Klein draft contract seen by Reuters asked the model to accept, for no extra pay, that the brand “may use reasonably unrecognizable images of Model (no identifying features such as Model's face, scars, tattoos or otherwise) to train and fine tune AI tools for learning general model attributes.” A Calvin Klein spokesperson said in a statement: "Like many others, we are testing and learning in this fast-moving space," adding that the brand's AI use is guided by regulation, industry standards and respect for models' rights. In many cases, contracts include wording such as "including" or "not limited to," which lawyers commonly use to claim rights that aren’t spelled out. Melanie Howard, partner and chair of luxury brands at law firm Loeb & Loeb in Los Angeles, represents both brands and talent in contract negotiations and said such sweeping language "is dangerous in its ambiguity” and makes it difficult for models to challenge any unsanctioned use of their images. In a photo-shoot contract seen by Reuters, France’s L'Oreal asked for "the right to use artificial intelligence (AI) technologies... including for the purpose of modifying, enhancing, or adapting the appearance of cosmetic products, packaging, or shades, as well as for retouching purposes." Without addressing that contract language, L'Oreal said it uses standard AI tools in post-production and editing that don't affect the model's image. 'WE ARE SAVING SO MUCH MONEY' Some firms are openly embracing AI to replace models and save money.  Europe's biggest online-fashion retailer, Zalando, has rapidly adopted AI-generated imagery for marketing content – and shut both its photo studios in Berlin last year. Fast-fashion retailer About You, which Zalando acquired in July last year, also closed its studio. Overall, Zalando cut more than 340 jobs, though the company said it retained some of those employees in other roles. Now, About You is launching its Scayle Studios business, which creates digital imagery for other retailers using AI-generated models and promises a more than 90 per cent production-cost reduction. Scayle has 130 brand clients and has generated 190,000 outfits in the last month, according to a company spokesperson. "We are saving so much money," said Julian Jansen, vice president of marketing at About You. "You've always had this super fast world of ecommerce, and this super slow traditional world of photo shoots, it didn't fit together in any way – and now with AI, it's a completely different scale." LITTLE REGULATION Regulations globally haven’t kept pace with the threat to models’ livelihoods, but the New York State Fashion Workers Act is one exception. The law has made it illegal since June 2025 for brands to create or modify replicas of models without their explicit consent.  "The misuse of models' images is not new, but with AI that problem is accelerated tenfold," said Sara Ziff, founder and executive director of the New York-based nonprofit Model Alliance, which backed the legislation. Ziff, herself a model for years, pushes for similar laws in other states and federally.  The British Fashion Model Agents Association has drawn up an AI code of practice, including that AI can only be used with the consent of a model, who would own any digital twin. But BFMA head John Horner said that without binding regulation in Britain or Europe, models still risk being taken advantage of by less scrupulous agents. "A lot of young talents don’t fully understand the long-term consequences yet," said Staal, the Barcelona-based model agency director. "Signing away AI rights at 20 years old could still affect someone ten years later."

Source: Reuters

item.title: Who controls powerful AI? Anthropic has a plan for long after its leaders depart
item.description: SAN FRANCISCO, Oct 27 : Few public companies claim to have the future of humanity on the line while making mundane choices about board composition.Not so with Anthropic. Having warned that its artificial intelligence could one day cure cancer or kill up to 8 billion people, Anthropic has set up a complex plan
item.dc:creator: CNA

Who controls powerful AI? Anthropic has a plan for long after its leaders depart

FAST

SAN FRANCISCO, Oct 27 : Few public companies claim to have the future of humanity on the line while making mundane choices about board composition. Not so with Anthropic. Having warned that its artificial intelligence could one day cure cancer or kill up to 8 billion people, Anthropic has set up a complex plan for who can govern the company as its technology rapidly progresses, its Monday IPO filing showed. Its expected $1.5 trillion valuation would make Anthropic the world's most highly valued public benefit corporation, a setup under Delaware law that means the AI lab must balance investor interests with promoting a wider good. More than fine print, Anthropic's setup may have big implications for investors and a public increasingly adopting the San Francisco-based company's AI. The details show how Anthropic has insulated itself from investor pressure so it can pursue what it says is best for humanity.

Anthropic gave 50.1 per cent voting power over certain matters to its seven co-founders, who, according to the filing, are "distinctly equipped to be stewards of our mission," Reuters previously reported. Though an independent trust will control a majority of board seats, the co-founders' supervoting power will extend to elections of the remaining directors and shareholder proposals generally. The Monday filing revealed still more intricacies to overseeing a business that Anthropic expects will outlive the tight-knit crew that created it. Once most of its co-founders are out of the picture and their "Class F" supervoting stock is gone, Anthropic's board will divide into three similarly sized groups, serving three-year terms. Staggering directors' reelection like in the US Senate, Anthropic has embraced a structure once popular as a way to stem hostile takeovers. The company has long voiced concern about the risks of AI falling into authoritarian or nefarious hands. That structure also goes against some corporate-governance tides. In this century, major US companies have largely moved to electing all directors annually, making companies more responsive to shareholder demands on areas like executive pay or strategy. Anthropic declined to comment. 'LONG-TERM FLEXIBILITY' Beyond its board, Anthropic has another governing body with its own set of rules: its long-term benefit trust. Currently chaired by global health leader Neil "Buddy" Shah, the trust controls a special share class called "Class T" stock that will let it elect a majority of Anthropic's board. Anthropic has contemplated what happens if that stock goes away, too. The goal of such eventualities is to "preserve long-term flexibility if circumstances change," its filing said. Even if someone not bound by Anthropic's mission to benefit humanity takes hold of its Class T stock, Anthropic's setup would require directors to follow "provisions relating to our public benefit purpose." Ultimately, the trust's power over the board makes Anthropic a "controlled company" under Nasdaq rules, exempting it from following some typical requirements like having an independent nominating and corporate governance committee. Anthropic is using that exemption to put Daniela Amodei, its president and sister of CEO Dario Amodei, on that committee. THE LEADERS IN CHARGE Anthropic set up a safety and risk committee on its board as well, currently made up of Novartis CEO Vas Narasimhan and former Trump White House official Chris Liddell. Billionaire Netflix co-founder Reed Hastings is Anthropic's current lead independent director. Still, Anthropic's seven co-founders — the Amodei siblings among them — remain at the core of governance for the foreseeable future. This partly is through the existence of an entity called "Founder LLC," which, after the trust, will have the biggest say in board elections.

Source: Reuters

item.title: Alibaba wins injunction against Pentagon contract restrictions tied to China blacklist
item.description: A US federal judge on Monday (Oct 27) granted Alibaba Group Holding's request for a preliminary injunction, ordering the US government not to deny Pentagon contracts to companies because they, their parent companies or subsidiaries do business with firms that engage in lobbying activities for the e-commerce giant.

FAST

A US federal judge on Monday (Oct 27) granted Alibaba Group Holding's request for a preliminary injunction, ordering the US government not to deny Pentagon contracts to companies because they, their parent companies or subsidiaries do business with firms that engage in lobbying activities for the e-commerce giant. Alibaba sued the US government in June after the Pentagon added it to a list of companies allegedly aiding China's military , alongside internet search provider Baidu, EV maker BYD and other major Chinese manufacturing and technology firms. Monday's ruling means Alibaba will be able to retain US lobbyists who also represent Pentagon contractors, removing a potential obstacle to the company's efforts to challenge its designation as a Chinese military company. Alibaba fired dozens of its Washington lobbyists after the Pentagon action in June, according to a source with direct knowledge of the matter who was not authorised to speak to the media.

The designation does not impose formal sanctions, but restricts Pentagon contracts with listed companies and, from 2027, purchases of their products or services through third parties. Other listed Chinese tech firms were also concerned about the designation's impact on international lobbying activities as well as the indirect procurement ban, which would completely remove Chinese products from US defence contractors' supply chains, the source added. Alibaba has denied any military ties, saying its products and services are built for retail, logistics, and enterprise technology rather than defence or intelligence. "The determinations have no basis in fact or law," Alibaba said in its lawsuit in June, seeking its removal from the list.

Related:

China 'strongly dissatisfied' with Pentagon move against top Chinese tech firms

Why Alibaba, Baidu and BYD are on Pentagon’s list of 'Chinese military companies'

Monday's injunction does not remove Alibaba from the Pentagon list, which the company is continuing to challenge in court. Alibaba did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the injunction. COMPANIES TAKE LEGAL ACTION Alibaba is one of several Chinese firms taking legal action to challenge their placement on the Pentagon's list. Last month, two subsidiaries of the world's largest electric vehicle maker BYD sued the US Department of Defence over a federal law banning any Pentagon contractors from hiring lobbyists that also work with blacklisted firms, arguing that it breached BYD's First Amendment rights. In August, DJI, the world's largest drone maker, appealed its inclusion on the blacklist with the court finding merit in its argument that unclassified records did not support the conclusion that the company contributed to the Chinese defence industrial base. The appeals court ordered the lower court to reconsider its decision to reject DJI's bid to be removed from the Pentagon list and the case is ongoing. The same month, biotech firm WuXi AppTec Co also won a preliminary injunction from a US federal court, which blocked its inclusion on the list. WuXi said the Pentagon designation was politically motivated.

Source: Reuters/ec

item.title: UPS CEO says delivery company will make more money on slightly fewer holiday deliveries
item.description: United Parcel Service raised its annual revenue and profit forecasts on Tuesday on better-than-expected third-quarter earnings after cutting doorstep deliveries of millions of unprofitable packages for Amazon.
item.dc:creator: Nandan Mandayam, Lisa Baertlein
item.content:encoded: United Parcel Service (UPS.N) raised its annual revenue and profit forecasts on Tuesday on better-than-expected third-quarter earnings after cutting doorstep deliveries of millions of unprofitable packages for Amazon. CEO Carol Tome said UPS' focus on more lucrative business means it can make more money delivering slightly fewer packages during its critical peak holiday season quarter every year. Shares of the world's largest parcel delivery firm jumped nearly 3% in early trading. Atlanta-based UPS expects total average daily volume to be down 1.3% in the fourth quarter as it becomes more selective in which packages it delivers. At the same time, executives forecast a roughly 3% rise in revenue in the company's domestic operation, its largest, and an estimated 7% increase in international revenue. "We're dispelling the old belief that all packages were created equal and that volume solves all problems," Tome told Reuters. A widening gap between the cost per parcel and revenue per parcel will improve margins, Chief Financial Officer Brian Dykes said. UPS' reduction in unprofitable deliveries — and the resulting lower volume reduction — in the fourth quarter means UPS can spend less on labor as well as truck and plane leases to handle the holiday package surge, Dykes said. Tome said the outlook for holiday delivery demand is strong as US consumers continue spending despite pressures from rising inflation and prices at the pump. "US consumers remain resilient," she said. SLIMMER OPERATION SETS STAGE FOR GROWTH UPS has shuttered facilities and shed thousands of jobs after scaling back deliveries for Amazon (AMZN.O) , its largest customer. UPS said it completed the Amazon scale-down in the second quarter. Rival FedEx (FDX.N) , which reports results on Wednesday, is using a similar strategy. Both companies have been under pressure from investors to improve margins by focusing on higher-value shipments. Tome also said data center construction is a significant opportunity as it touches every part of UPS, which can fly in critical components such as microprocessors, arrange ocean shipments of equipment, store goods and make final deliveries. For the third quarter, UPS posted adjusted profit of $1.69 per share, lower than $1.74 per share a year ago but above analysts' average estimate of $1.63. Third-quarter adjusted operating margin in UPS' domestic unit, which generates about 65% of company revenue, rose to 7% from 6.4% a year earlier. The smaller but more profitable international package division also reported a higher adjusted operating margin of 14.9% for the third quarter, compared with 14.8% last year. Jefferies analysts said third-quarter earnings showcased a "quarter of strong execution," while Evercore ISI analyst Jonathan Chappell wrote in a note that the results give "some confidence in durability." UPS also said it was on track to meet its target of $3 billion in cost savings this year. It has saved $1.8 billion through September. The company now expects 2026 adjusted profit of around $7.28 per share, compared with the $7.22 it had forecast in July. Analysts expect the company to report a profit of $7.19 per share, according to data compiled by LSEG. UPS expects annual revenue of $92.6 billion, compared with its previous projection of $91.2 billion and above analysts' estimate of $91.73 billion.

item.title: 中国、中東に近く特使派遣へ 紛争の波及・拡大を懸念
item.description: [北京 ２７日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[北京 ２７日 ロイター] - 中国外務省の郭嘉昆報道官は２７日の定例記者会見で、中東および周辺地域における紛争を深く懸念しているとして、関係各国に特使を近く派遣すると明らかにした。

関係各国に対し、対話と交渉を通じて意見の相違を解決するよう呼びかけたほか、中東の紛争がアフリカの角や紅海地域へ波及・拡大することへの懸念も表明。「中国は間もなく特使を派遣し、当該地域の各国を訪問して関係諸国との意思疎通を強化し、接触と対話を促進し、緊張緩和を図り、事態のさらなる悪化を防ぐ」と述べた。

item.title: Bond investors are thinking less about the Fed and more about AI, deficits
item.description: Wall Street considers it settled that the Federal Reserve will hold interest rates steady this week. Whether that spells good news for Treasuries is more complicated.
item.dc:creator: Gertrude Chavez-Dreyfuss
item.content:encoded: Wall Street considers it settled that the Federal Reserve will hold interest rates steady this week. Whether that spells good news for Treasuries is more complicated. After a bruising selloff that took yields up sharply for two months starting in August, the Treasury market has rallied, reflecting concern that financing troubles in a corner of the market [USN:l6n4690sj TEXT:"for AI infrastructure"] could slow the artificial intelligence buildout that is a central driver of the US economy. Yields [USN:l6n4681a9 TEXT:"have come down from the highs"] they hit early in October. But analysts and portfolio managers stress that many of the forces that have [USN:l6n45n0y4 TEXT:"made bond investors miserable this year"] — stubborn inflation, heavy government and corporate borrowing, and uncertainty over next week's [TOPIC:"reuters:/world/us/elections/" TEXT:"midterm elections"] — remain in place. That makes it difficult to forecast what the rest of 2026 holds for a market where prices are still down significantly for the year. "I don't think the Fed is entirely in the driver's seat in today's market. Increasingly, the bigger story is the AI-driven investment cycle and what happens to risk sentiment around it," said Christian Hoffmann, head of fixed income at Thornburg Investment Management. "In recent trading, capital has moved out of some AI-related trades and into bonds in what looks like a flight to quality, and flows like that can overwhelm relatively small changes in Fed expectations." FEW EXPECT A RATE INCREASE Investors expect the Fed to stay on hold but to raise rates again in December. The decision may be less important than what officials signal about inflation and the path of rates in the months ahead, investors said. Markets have repeatedly swung between expectations for policy easing and tightening on concerns that persistent price pressures could force the Fed to keep borrowing costs elevated for longer. The benchmark 10-year yield has risen 84 basis points this year, on track for its largest yearly increase since 2022. US 30-year yields are up nearly 50 basis points in 2026, their biggest yearly rise since 2024. Of late, comments from Fed officials John Williams and Philip Jefferson [USN:l6n46518p TEXT:"helped to reset investor expectations towards fewer near-term rate hikes"]. Both sit on the policy-making Federal Open Market Committee. But few have forgotten that consumer and producer prices rose in August and September, with higher energy prices -- which remain elevated -- as one of the main culprits. "Inflation has clearly re-accelerated so to us this isn't necessarily a pause, but just to see how some of this data changes given the recent hike," said Jack Herr, senior investment analyst at GuideStone Funds. "The Fed will probably hike again this year." FISCAL HEADWINDS Even if the Fed stays on hold, the long end of the curve -- bonds with maturities of 10 or more years -- could remain under pressure. JPMorgan's latest Treasury Client Survey showed client positioning with the fewest outright longs since mid-August, reflecting reduced betting on lower yields. That outlook reflects in part the government's growing financing need, with a worsening fiscal backdrop and the $40 trillion national debt contributing to bouts of volatility. Treasury issuance has surged alongside widening budget deficits, increasing the amount of debt that private investors must absorb. The steady increase in supply has become an important driver of longer-term yields and has at times overshadowed changes in Fed policy expectations. "It's hard to have a lot of confidence in exactly what's going to happen from here, especially when you're looking at ongoing deficits on the order of 6% of GDP (gross domestic product)," said Chris Maxey, chief market strategist at Wealthspire. "Our net debt interest costs could actually consume more of our deficit, and that begins to squeeze out other spending that happens. That could naturally push yields higher across the curve because there's just that fiscal concern element." Many investors took the intensity of the late summer bond rout as a shot across the bow of policy makers, but even those who believe the message was received say it will take time to change the momentum on spending in Washington. "Regardless of the election results, we should not probably expect any meaningful fiscal restraint," said Oli Shale, US investment specialist at asset manager Ruffer. "More spending is the path of least resistance and this regime is not going anywhere for some time." (This story has been refiled to change the company name to 'Wealthspire,' not 'Wealthspire Advisors,' in paragraph 13. )

item.title: Crypto blitzes midterms with $176 million to support allies as it prepares for post-Trump era
item.description: The crypto industry has spent roughly $176 million across more than 100 midterm races this election cycle, as part of a years-long plan to build a bipartisan coalition of allies in Congress that can advance its interests long after US President Donald Trump leaves office.
item.dc:creator: Dawn Kopecki
item.content:encoded: The crypto industry has spent roughly $176 million across more than 100 midterm races this election cycle, as part of a years-long plan to build a bipartisan coalition of allies in Congress that can advance its interests long after US President Donald Trump leaves office. The $2.75 trillion industry, and the billionaires who built it, are aggressively spending to elect friendly candidates while targeting politicians they see as a threat, according to interviews with more than a half-dozen crypto political strategists and a Reuters review of the spending. While the industry’s recent spending blitz is known, its long-term plan to further its legislative agenda is less well-understood. The industry isn’t just looking for allies; it is trying to pick candidates who already have a chance of winning, and can help once they get to Congress, the strategists said. Crypto's largest super political action committee, Fairshake, which spent $196 million during the 2024 election cycle, is leading the industry’s strategy again. Fairshake said 53 of the 58 candidates it supported in primaries or special elections this year won and will be on the ballot on November 3. Super PACs can accept and spend unlimited sums of money, but cannot coordinate directly with campaigns. They are flooding several races with tens of millions of dollars in ads. Voters have little way of knowing who pays for these ads, which barely mention crypto. Most of Fairshake's are sponsored by its affiliate PACs with innocuous names like "Defend American Jobs" and "Protect Progress." The ads often focus on hot-button issues like taxes or immigration. Perceived enemies, such as longtime skeptic Sherrod Brown, vying to return to the Senate in Ohio, can be subjected to an onslaught of often-personal attacks. Advocacy group Public Citizen said crypto was the single-biggest corporate spender in federal races in 2026, after saying in 2024 that its spending was "akin to a corporate Death Star hovering over elections." The PACs' primary financiers, led by Coinbase, Ripple and venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz, aren't trying to convince voters to support digital currencies. The money is a calling card to help forge long-term relationships with elected officials, said industry strategists, campaign staff, watchdog groups and political finance managers. It underscores how the industry is behaving as other businesses do in Washington — using funds to open doors and buffer itself against regulation. The strategy reflects the reality that come 2029, the occupant of the White House is unlikely to be as personally invested in crypto as Trump, whose family made around $2.3 billion from crypto ventures between mid-2024 and April, a Reuters investigation found . “It's an investment in the future,” said Colin McLaren, head of government relations at crypto industry advocacy group the Solana Policy Institute, which has given $4.9 million to the midterms this year, according to campaign finance records. The effort is designed to “ensure that over the next 100 years, the crypto industry has clear rules of the road, and that we know what our regulators are expecting from us," he said. Through October 20, Fairshake and its affiliate PACs have spent about $150.8 million on the midterms this year, while other crypto groups have spent around $25 million, according to campaign finance filings. "We back pro-crypto candidates who support American innovation in both parties, and look forward to continuing to build on the largest pro-crypto caucus in American history," said Geoff Vetter, spokesperson for Fairshake. COME A LONG WAY In 2018, lawmakers couldn’t even get a room in the House or Senate office buildings to hold the first congressional bipartisan roundtable discussion on crypto, instead meeting across the street from the US Capitol in the Library of Congress, said Kristin Smith, president of the Solana Policy Institute, who helped establish the Blockchain Association that year. The Biden administration heavily scrutinized the industry following the collapse of FTX and an [USN:L3N2X40RX TEXT:"industry-wide meltdown"] in 2022, with the US Securities and Exchange Commission eventually levying more than $6 billion in penalties in 98 cases, according to a Georgetown University Law study. “It was an all-out assault on the technology,” said Smith, the Blockchain Association's interim CEO. “The industry was in a corner, and the only way out was to show political force.” Executives decided they needed a political strategy to combat what they called then-SEC chair Gary Gensler’s “regulation by enforcement,” lobbyists, advocacy groups and campaign strategists said. Coinbase Chief Policy Officer Faryar Shirzad was the architect behind nonprofit political advocacy group Stand With Crypto — which isn't required to disclose its donors — and Fairshake, which both launched in 2023. The number of Congresspeople with an "A" rating from Stand With Crypto is up to 332, compared with 96 when the group launched. As the industry has won more legal clarity in Washington, its market value has nearly tripled from around $1 trillion in 2023 to about $2.75 trillion now, according to CoinGecko . The combination of Trump, a growing bipartisan congressional coalition and a neutered opposition allowed the industry to advance its legislative agenda more in the last two years than some industries have done in decades, other industry lobbyists say. That includes 2025's Genius Act legislation establishing the first-ever US federal regulatory framework for stablecoins, enacted with overwhelming bipartisan support. That followed a White House meeting earlier in the year when industry leaders, including Coinbase (COIN.O) CEO Brian Armstrong and Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse, [USN:L2N3PP0UZ TEXT:"sat with Trump"] when the president declared an end to the "war on crypto." "Moving that quickly in Washington is like light speed in space," said Ron Bonjean, partner at bipartisan public affairs firm Rokk Solutions, and a former senior Senate aide. The industry's real goal is passing the Clarity Act, which would put crypto oversight under the Commodity Futures Trading Commission. That bill stalled in this congressional session and faces an uphill battle next year if Democrats win control of one or more chambers of Congress. Without it, agency-level [USN:FWN45Q05G TEXT:"regulations undertaken during Trump's term"] can be reversed by a subsequent administration, analysts at JPMorgan said. Fairshake is financing House candidates from both parties, but it decided to only back Republicans in Senate races after Democrats in that chamber blocked the Clarity Act from advancing to a final vote. Their opposition centered around an ethics provision that would have forced the Trump family to sell their crypto holdings. Gary Kalman, of anti-corruption nonprofit Transparency International, criticized the bill for shifting regulation to the less-stringent CFTC, and for preempting states from enacting tougher laws. Coinbase and Andreessen Horowitz declined to comment. Ripple didn't return requests for comment. THE PRIME TARGET Fairshake's highest-profile win in 2024 was defeating Brown, an industry foe who chaired the Senate Banking Committee from 2021 to 2024. Spending millions attacking the sitting chairman of the industry's oversight committee was unprecedented in Washington, corporate watchdogs and political strategists say. But the gamble paid off. Now, Brown is running again, with public opinion polls showing him with a narrow lead over his opponent, Republican Jon Husted. The industry has spent more than $68 million on the race, helping to make it one of the most expensive on record, according to AdImpact. Fairshake’s ads opposing Brown, which it did not comment on, don't mention crypto. One charges him with voting to raise gas taxes in Ohio and raises a [USN:L1N2ZT27M TEXT:"Reuters-debunked claim"] that he voted to "unleash 87,000 IRS agents on you while voting to give social security benefits to illegals." “Of course, the special interests are panicking, they know Sherrod will fight the rigged system they're feasting on to stand up for working Ohioans,” said Patrick Eisenhauer, Brown's campaign manager. A CRYPTO MONEY BOMB In some races, crypto spending dwarfed candidate fundraising. The industry spent $5.3 million in a Maryland House Democratic primary to support state Delegate Adrian Boafo, who raised $1.9 million on his own, records show. Other non-crypto groups spent $6.8 million to support Boafo's campaign, which declined to comment. “There were so many ads ... that it makes other candidates suffocate,” said Quincy Bareebe, a healthcare entrepreneur who came in second of 24 candidates in that primary despite spending $6.6 million of her own money. "Adrian was everywhere." The industry was less successful in Illinois. Fairshake spent over $10.1 million on ads attacking [USN:L1N4001C8 TEXT:"Lieutenant Governor Juliana Stratton"], who is running for US Senate, and another $2.5 million against Illinois state Representative La Shawn Ford, who is running for a Chicago-area congressional district. Both are expected to win on November 3. Ford defeated a dozen primary challengers despite raising just $500,000 and lending his campaign $175,000 to fight off industry-funded ads that brought up a 14-year-old federal indictment that was later dropped. His campaign issued a cease-and-desist letter to Fairshake, accusing it of making defamatory statements about him in its ads. Fairshake did not comment on its ads or Ford's response. Ford thinks Fairshake targeted him because he supported state legislation to require crypto exchanges and related companies to register with Illinois. “They were relentless, on every outlet, radio, TV, social media, mailers," Ford said. “It was personal and it was hurtful, and unnecessary for my family to have to go through.”

item.title: 北欧首脳、プーチン氏と電話会談 ウクライナ巡り協議
item.description:
Essi Lehto
[ヘルシンキ／キーウ／モスクワ ２７日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Essi Lehto

[ヘルシンキ／キーウ／モスクワ　２７日　ロイター] - フィンランドのストゥブ大統領とノルウェーのストーレ首相は２７日、ロシアのプーチン大統領と電話会談し、ウクライナ戦争の終結を促した。ロシア大統領との直接対話を避けてきた西欧諸国首脳の慣行から転換した。

今回の電話会談は、トランプ米大統領がロシア寄りに立場を変え、米国とウクライナの関係が過去１８カ月で最も悪化する中で行われた。ウクライナのシビハ外相によると、電話会談はウクライナと調整の上で実施。ストーレ氏は全てのパートナー国と同盟国に事前に通知したとしている。

ストーレ氏によると、プーチン氏と約９０分間にわたり電話会談を行った後、ウクライナのゼレンスキー大統領と協議を行った。ストーレ氏とストゥブ氏は共同声明で、今回の電話会談は来月アブダビで予定されているロシア、ウクライナ、米国の当局者による和平協議につながるものになると説明。３カ国当局者による協議は２月以来となる。

両首脳は共同声明で「（プーチン氏との）議論は率直で実質的だった。われわれはロシアの隣国だ。この戦争の結末は、われわれ両国と欧州全体の安全保障に直接影響する。戦争を終結させるには直接対話が必要だ」と表明した。ストーレ氏は「戦争は人的にも物的にも甚大な損失をもたらしている。苦しみと破壊は世代を超えて影響を及ぼす。電話会談では緊張緩和の重要性を強調した」と述べた。

両首脳はウクライナへの強力な支持を強調、支援を継続すると表明した。

＜ロシア側に妥協の兆しなし＞

ロシア大統領府が公表した電話会談の概要からは、プーチン氏に妥協する姿勢はうかがえない。大統領府は「ロシア連邦の正当な利益が全面的かつ無条件に考慮されて初めて、公正で長期的な平和の実現が可能になると強調した」と説明。同時に「欧州連合（ＥＵ）と北大西洋条約機構（ＮＡＴＯ）加盟国の対立的な政策が戦闘の長期化を助長していることにも注意が向けられた」とした。

ロシアのラブロフ外相は、今回の電話会談で何も新たなことは示されなかったとし、欧州諸国は交渉プロセスで一定の役割を確保しようとしているにすぎないとの見方を示した。

ただ、ロシア大統領府によると、プーチン氏、ストゥブ氏、ストーレ氏は今後も電話で連絡を取り合うことで一致した。

＜ウクライナと調整の上で実施＞

ウクライナのシビハ外相は、ゼレンスキー大統領がフィンランドとノルウェーの首脳に対し、停戦の必要性とウクライナとロシアの首脳会談の実現をプーチン氏に伝えるよう要請したと明らかにした上で、今回の電話会談はウクライナとの調整の上で実施されたもので、適切だったと指摘。「ウクライナの外交努力と和平プロセスに対する、こうした積極的な支援を歓迎する」と述べた。

＜デンマーク首相、北欧２首脳の電話会談を批判＞

デンマークのフレデリクセン首相は、フィンランドとノルウェーのプーチン氏との対話を批判。ロシアが平和を望んでいる兆候は見られないとし、「欧州は個別に行動するのではなく、結束すべきだと思う」と語った。

ストゥブ、ストーレ両氏は、それぞれ自国の首脳として電話会談に参加したのであり、欧州全体を代表して発言したわけではないと説明。両国は長年にわたるウクライナ支援を継続するとした。

ロシアはこれまで、欧州各国政府がウクライナに武器を供与し、直接対話を拒むことで戦争をあおっていると繰り返し非難してきた。また西欧諸国の首脳の姿勢を、プーチン氏と対話し、これまでのところ成果は出ていないものの和平合意の仲介を試みてきたトランプ氏の姿勢と対比させている。

ロシア大統領府の関係筋はロイターに対し、プーチン氏と最後に電話会談したＥＵ首脳はフランスのマクロン大統領だったと述べた。同筋によると、２０２６年７月に行われた会談は公表されず、成果もなかった。

関係者によると、プーチン氏はストゥブ、ストーレ両氏に、ウクライナ東部ドンバス地域全域の掌握という目標についてロシアは妥協しないと伝えた。これに対し、両氏は「公正な」平和が必要だと応じたという。

ストーレ氏とストゥブ氏は先週、オスロでウィットコフ米和平交渉担当特使、ウクライナのゼレンスキー大統領と会談。ウィットコフ氏はその翌日、ロシア第２の都市サンクトペテルブルクでプーチン氏と会談した。ロシア大統領府はプーチン氏とウィットコフ氏の会談後、米国が仲介するウクライナとの和平協議を１１月に再開する意向を表明していた。

item.title: ＵＢＳ、外部ＡＩによる顧客代行の操作認めず＝ＣＥＯ
item.description: [チューリヒ ２７日 ロイター] - スイスの金融大手ＵＢＳのセルジオ・エルモッティ最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は２７日、...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ＵＢＳ、外部ＡＩによる顧客代行の操作認めず＝ＣＥＯ 10/27 18:58 配信

スイスの金融大手ＵＢＳのロゴ。4月22日、スイスのベルンで撮影。REUTERS/Denis Balibouse（ロイター） [チューリヒ ２７日 ロイター] - スイスの金融大手ＵＢＳのセルジオ・エルモッティ最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は２７日、外部の人工知能（ＡＩ）モデルに顧客の代わりに行動させることは認めないと述べた。

銀行業界では、高度なＡＩエージェントが金融システムに悪影響を及ぼしかねないとの懸念が高まっている。関係者によると、米大手銀行は外部のＡＩエージェントによる顧客口座へのアクセスを遮断している。

エルモッティ氏は科学関連の会議で「最近、一部の銀行では、顧客口座の管理や預金の移動、最適化に当たってＡＩモデルが不適切に動作するリスクがあるという話を耳にしただろう。われわれはＡＩモデルが銀行にアクセスしてそうした操作を行うことを認めていない」と述べた。

ＡＩについて今最も重要なのは、判断の過程が見えないまま顧客に影響を及ぼすＡＩモデルを使わないようにすることだと語った。

また２０２３年に買収したクレディ・スイスとの統合に伴い、ＵＢＳはＡＩの導入ペースをやや落とさざるを得なかったが、現在は技術に一段と注力できるようになったと説明した。

「統合がほぼ完了したことをうれしく思う。これにより技術をどう活用して銀行の業務の実効性と効率を高めるかに、さらに力を入れられる」と述べた。

ロイター 関連リンク 焦点：米経済へのＡＩ効果、潜在成長率への波及は不透明 コラム：ＩＭＦが指摘する「薄氷のＡＩ相場」、日本も逆資産効果に備える時か＝唐鎌大輔氏 アングル：ＡＩ関連の資金調達、低格付け領域にも拡大　投資家は警戒感強める コラム：ベセント氏の危うい賭け、ＡＩ主導の経済成長は「債務病」の特効薬ならず コラム：ＩＴサービス企業、生成ＡＩ追い風に株価上昇か 10/27(火) 18:58 最終更新 ロイター

item.title: メルセデス・ベンツ、主力部門利益率見通し下げ 中国低迷などで
item.description: [２７日 ロイター] - ドイツの高級車メーカー、メルセデス・ベンツは２７日、中国における市場環境の厳しさが増して...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
メルセデス・ベンツ、主力部門利益率見通し下げ　中国低迷などで 10/27 18:56 配信

メルセデス・ベンツのロゴ。2025年7月に撮影。REUTERS/Dado Ruvic（ロイター） [２７日 ロイター] - ドイツの高級車メーカー、メルセデス・ベンツは２７日、中国における市場環境の厳しさが増していることや第４・四半期のコスト増を理由に、主力事業である乗用車部門の２０２６年利益率見通しを２─３％に引き下げた。従来は３─５％を見込んでいた。

グループ営業利益見通しも下方修正し、大幅な増益ではなく、前年比でほぼ横ばいになると予想している。

メルセデスの主力となる乗用車販売は、中国での需要低迷の影響を受け、第３・四半期に前年同期比８％減となった。
